items.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played with Kenny Burrell in ’50 when I returned... for a while, maybe a year-and-a half.

ctx.x: ...playing with Cab Calloway. Um...so every Monday we’d look forward to just standing in front of the bandstand. Uh...and...at the same time, within the city was people like Kenny Burrell–Billy Burrell was his brother, and he he taught Kenny how to play the guitar–and, low and behold, from Saginaw [Michigan] came Sonny Stitt. He would come down to Detroit frequently. Uh...he was a remarkable saxophonist. I often think of how to define him, but he was such a perfectionist, uh and he wasn’t braggadocious about it.…

items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yusef Lateef, who I worked with and while we were working I was at Wayne State.

ctx.x: Yeah, so it was cool. So I thank him, and I saw him later, you know, I used to see him. He’s passed on now, but I used to see him an always like Bags and Milt and Al would always thank him. My brother Billy went to that high school, he knew Billy. Yusef Lateef went there, his name was Bill Evans at the time, went to that same high school. Eddie Locke…I can’t think of his name right now, the other bop…
